title: Composable routing policy primitives for version pinning, canary weighting, and deterministic fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we roll out model versions and run canary/A-B experiments, interactions between region selection, tier routing (hosted vs dedicated), and model variant fallbacks are producing surprising routing decisions and increased p99 latency for small subsets of traffic. Current routing logic is monolithic and interleaves: region affinity, tier preference, session pin TTL, and ad-hoc canary splits. This makes it hard to reason about correctness, produce deterministic audits, or safely implement gradual rollouts with TTL-based session pinning and deterministic fallbacks.

Goal: Introduce a set of composable routing primitives and a deterministic evaluation order that: 1) preserves session pinning semantics during canary/A-B rollouts, 2) guarantees a reproducible fallback matrix when a pinned variant is unavailable, 3) supports cost-aware tier preference and region constraints, and 4) emits structured telemetry to validate rollout behavior and SLO impact.

Scope: Design and implement the primitives in the routing resolver + rollout controller; add unit and e2e tests; integrate telemetry in Console dashboards and rollout audit logs; provide a migration plan for existing rollout configs. Not in scope: UI changes to Console (separate design ticket) and backend autoscaling changes (follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Routing resolver exposes modular primitives: Affinity(pin-by-session), CanarySplit(weight), TierPriority(hosted,dedicated,private), RegionConstraint(preferred,excluded), FallbackStrategy(fallback-to-compatible-variant, degrade-to-cheaper-quantized).
Deterministic evaluation order documented and enforced: 1) RegionConstraint, 2) TierPriority, 3) Affinity (session pin TTL), 4) CanarySplit, 5) FallbackStrategy.
Session pin TTL behavior: pinned sessions stick to variant for TTL unless forced by admin rollout; pinned variant unavailability triggers a deterministic fallback path with emitted reason codes.
Telemetry events for each routing decision available in Console: route.chosen_variant, route.fallback_reason, route.latency_estimate, route.cost_estimate, route.traffic_bucket.
End-to-end tests that simulate region outage and capacity shortage with assertions for deterministic fallbacks and no traffic loss beyond configured degrade policy.
tasks: Design RFC describing primitives, evaluation order, fallbacks and API contract (link to doc)
Implement routing primitives in resolver (C++/Rust module) and expose config protobufs
Add rollout controller changes to compute stable hashing for canary buckets and session pin affinity
Instrument telemetry and add Console audit log events
Integration tests: deterministic routing harness that replays historical traffic across multiple regions/tiers
PR + code review and staging rollout behind feature flag
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Created initial RFC draft and shared with runtime and platform teams. Added proposed primitive names and a sketch of evaluation order. Asked for early feedback on determinism guarantees.

2026-02-17 - Marco Chen: Reviewed RFC. Major concern: current KV cache pin semantics will interact with session pin. Proposed change: make routing decisions that affect cache-keying emit a kvcache.invalidate event and annotate session pins with cache compatibility metadata.
2026-02-21 - Priya Ramesh (SRE): SLO note: when fallback routes cross to dedicated we need cost and capacity tags and a circuit-breaker to avoid overwhelming dedicated pool during region degradation.
2026-02-25 - Marco Chen: Prototype of deterministic hash-based canary bucket completed (see PR). Added deterministic salt per rollout and stable hashing function to avoid churn when adding variants.
2026-03-02 - Design review (Riley O'Connor): UX needs a clear audit entry for 'sticky pin' vs 'forced override' to avoid confusion in Console rollout logs. Filed DES follow-up ticket.

2026-03-05 - QA (Daniel Park): Added test cases for concurrent multi-model requests (composed prompts) that must respect per-model pinning and single-request atomic routing. Found race where two per-model pins could mismatch; added a unit test that fails on current trunk.

2026-03-08 - Marco Chen: Implemented fallback matrix priority: compatible-variant-in-same-region -> compatible-variant-in-preferred-tier -> quantized-cheaper-variant -> regional-degrade->global-fallback. Emitting route.fallback_reason with codes: COMPATIBLE_REGION, COMPATIBLE_TIER, QUANTIZED, REGIONAL_DEGRADE, GLOBAL_FALLBACK.

2026-03-10 - Security review (Ana Gomez): No secrets exposed. Recommend adding an RBAC guard for change rollout weight API. Marked security_review_required=false but added note to product to gate API behind org-admin role.

2026-03-12 - Marco Chen: Merged core resolver PR behind feature flag 'composable-routing-v2'. Staging rollout scheduled. Next: integrate telemetry with Console and run regression test suite across 3 regions.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: keeping evaluation order deterministic reduces some expressivity (cannot prefer short-latency tier over session pin without explicit override). We prefer safety and auditability for rollouts.

Open question: whether TTL decay for session pins should use exponential decay on sticky affinity to avoid long-term entrenchment during long multi-week rollouts. Proposal: default TTL=7d with optional decay policy per rollout.
Follow-ups: DES ticket for Console audit UX, ENG ticket for autoscaling backpressure integration, PM ticket to document migration timeline for existing rollouts.
